A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:
(A) An application screening process that complies with all of the following:
(i) Completed applications are considered, as provided for in the landlord’s established screening criteria, in the order in which the completed applications were received. The landlord’s screening criteria shall be provided to the applicant in writing together with the application form.
(ii) The first applicant who meets the landlord’s established screening criteria is approved for tenancy.
(iii) Applicants are not
charged an application screening fee unless or until their application is actually considered.
rules.requirement: A landlord or their agent may charge a fee only if they offer an application screening process that considers completed applications in the order received, approves the first applicant meeting established criteria, provides criteria in writing, and charges fees only when applications are actually considered.

rules.quoted_span:
Legal Reasons for Eviction
Tenant is at-fault
Failure to pay rent
Failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement
Creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit
Using the rental unit for an illegal purpose
Failure to renew a similar rental agreement
Failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit
The person at the end of the lease term is a subtenant not approved by the landlord
Tenant is not at-fault
The owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit
A resident manager will move into the rental unit
Demolition and permanent removal from the rental market
Government order
Conversion to affordable housing
rules.requirement: Evictions under the RSO must be for legal reasons specified in the ordinance, including both at-fault reasons (failure to pay rent, lease violations, nuisance, illegal use, failure to renew, denied access, unapproved subtenant) and no-fault reasons (owner occupancy, manager occupancy, demolition, government order, conversion to affordable housing).

tenant’s lease or on January 31,  if the tenant has been given written notice, that the interest

one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional

rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit above 1.5 times one month's rent. Yearly increases may not exceed 10% of the current deposit.

rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental properties are covered.
rules.key_value: three business days after judgment for possession
rules.quoted_span:
The warrant for possession may not be issued unt il three (3) business 
days after the judgment for possession is granted. The tenant has three (3) business days to move 
all persons and belongings from the premises. If the tenant does not move after three (3) business 
days from the time the warrant for possession was served on the tenant, the landlord may arrange 
for the Court Officer to have the tenant evicted or locked out (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-57).
rules.requirement: After a judgment for possession is granted, the warrant for possession may not be issued until three business days after judgment. The tenant has three business days to move all persons and belongings from the premises after the warrant for possession is served.
rules.title: Warrant for Possession and Moving Timeline

rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental properties are covered.
rules.quoted_span:
A tenant may ask the court for permission to stay in the premises due to special 
circumstances that moving may cause. This action is a stay of eviction. If permission is granted, 
the tenant may not stay in the premises for more than one year, unless there is an agreed upon 
extension between landlord and tenant . All rent due ordinarily must be paid for permission to be 
granted by the court (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-59.1).
rules.requirement: A tenant may request a stay of eviction from the court due to special circumstances. If permission is granted, the tenant may remain for up to one year unless an extension is agreed upon by landlord and tenant. All rent due ordinarily must be paid for permission to be granted.
rules.title: Stay of Eviction

rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to 
prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.
rules.requirement: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant. No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease without good cause. For nonpayment of rent evictions, the landlord may file suit immediately; for other good cause evictions, a Notice to Quit must be served before filing suit.
rules.title: Good Cause Eviction Requirement

rules.coverage_conditions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are covered.

rules.quoted_span:
Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when 
a court issues an order for eviction. However, in these cases, the landlord must prove that the tenant 
(a) is staying after the expiration of the term of the lease, (b) is staying after a failure to pay rent, 
(c) is disorderly so as to destroy the peace and quiet of other tena nts, (d) willfully destroys or 
damages the premises, (e) constantly violates the written rules and regulations or (f) violates any 
lease provision where the lease reserves a right of re -entry for such violations.
rules.requirement: In owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, tenants can only be removed by court order on the following grounds: staying after lease expiration, failing to pay rent, disorderly conduct, willful destruction, constantly violating written rules, or violating lease provisions with reserved right of re-entry. Notice periods vary by tenancy type and cause.
rules.title: Eviction in Owner-Occupied Two or Three-Family Dwellings

rules.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Inquiry into conviction for drug-related criminal activity for manufacture or production of methamphetamine on premises of federally assisted housing; Inquiry into whether applicant is subject to lifetime registration requirement under State sex offender registration program
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer,
except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been
convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production
of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether
the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State
sex offender registration program.
rules.requirement: A housing provider must not require applicants to answer questions about criminal records before making a conditional offer, with narrow exceptions for methamphetamine manufacturing on federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registration requirements.
rules.title: Prohibition on criminal record inquiries before conditional offer

rules.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.quoted_span:
The housing provider shall perform an
individualized assessment of the application in light of the following factors:
(a)   the nature and severity of the criminal offense;
(b)   the age of the applicant at the time of the
occurrence of the criminal offense;
(c)   the time which has elapsed since the occurrence
of the criminal offense;
(d)   any information produced by the applicant, or
produced on the applicant's behalf, in regard to the applicant's rehabilitation
and good conduct since the occurrence of the criminal offense;
(e)   the degree to which the criminal offense, if it
reoccurred, would negatively impact the safety of the housing provider's other
tenants or property; and
(f)   whether the criminal offense occurred on or was
connected to property that was rented or leased by the applicant.
rules.requirement: When withdrawing a conditional offer, a housing provider must perform an individualized assessment considering: nature and severity of offense, applicant's age at time of offense, time elapsed, rehabilitation evidence, potential safety impact, and whether offense was connected to rental property.
rules.title: Required individualized assessment factors for criminal record withdrawal

rules.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that
explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant
who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except
for
drug-related criminal activity for the
manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally
assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime
registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.
rules.requirement: A housing provider must not knowingly publish housing advertisements stating it will not consider applicants with arrests or convictions, except for limited exceptions regarding methamphetamine manufacturing and sex offender registration.
rules.title: Prohibition on discriminatory housing advertisements regarding criminal records

$1,000 per violation of this Division, in a civil action against a landlord.

rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental properties subject to SDMC Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7.
rules.interaction: Governs over CA-JCE-02 where it applies (local law over state law).
rules.key_value: requires vacating the residential rental property for at least 30 days
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord seeks to recover possession to comply with any of the 
following:  
(A) an order issued by a government agency or court relating to 
habitability that requires vacating the residential rental 
property for at least 30 days. An order issued by a government 
agency or court relating to habitability that requires vacating 
the residential rental property for fewer than 30 days is not 
grounds to terminate a tenancy for just cause and a landlord 
may be required by applicable state or federal law to provide 
tenant relocation benefits; 
(B) an order issued by a government agency or court to vacate the 
residential rental property; or  
(C) a local ordinance that requires vacating the residential rental 
property.
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a tenancy for no-fault just cause to recover possession to comply with a government agency or court order requiring vacating for habitability issues for at least 30 days, or to comply with a government order to vacate, or to comply with a local ordinance requiring vacating. Tenants are not entitled to relocation assistance if found at fault for the condition.
rules.title: No-Fault Just Cause - Habitability Compliance

rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental properties subject to SDMC Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7.
rules.interaction: Governs over CA-JCE-02 where it applies (local law over state law).
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall provide 
written notice in no less than 12-point font to the tenant, and in a manner that 
complies with California Civil Code section 1632, as may be amended, that 
states as follows: 
California law limits the amount your rent can be increased. See 
California Civil Code section 1947.12 for more information. Local law 
also provides that a landlord shall provide a statement of cause in any 
notice to terminate a tenancy. In some circumstances, tenants who are 
seniors (62 years or older) or disabled may be entitled to additional 
tenant protections. See Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 of the San 
Diego Municipal Code for more information. 
 
(b) A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall include 
a copy of the Tenant Protection Guide with the written notice required by 
section 98.0705(a).
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants written notice in 12-point font complying with California Civil Code section 1632 stating that California law limits rent increases and citing section 1947.12, and that local law requires cause statements in termination notices, with additional protections for seniors and disabled tenants. The notice must include a Tenant Protection Guide prepared by the San Diego Housing Commission. For existing tenancies, notice must be provided within 90 days of June 24, 2023. For new or renewed tenancies from June 24, 2023 onward, notice must be included in the lease or as a signed document.
rules.title: Notice to Tenant of Residential Tenant Protections

rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental properties subject to SDMC Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7.
rules.interaction: Governs over CA-JCE-02 where it applies (local law over state law).
rules.quoted_span:
Before a landlord issues a notice to terminate a 
tenancy for at-fault just cause that is a curable lease violation, the 
landlord shall first give written notice of the violation including a 
description of the violation and an opportunity to cure the violation 
under California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161(3), as may be 
amended. If the violation is not cured within the time period in the 
notice, the landlord may terminate the tenancy without another 
opportunity to cure by serving a three-day notice to quit.
rules.requirement: For at-fault just cause terminations that are curable lease violations, the landlord must first give written notice of the violation with a description and opportunity to cure. If not cured within the specified time, the landlord may serve a three-day notice to quit. The landlord must notify the Commission in writing no later than three business days after notice to tenant.
rules.title: Notice Requirements for At-Fault Just Cause Termination
